In a backstage dressing room of a traditional theater, a performer sits in front of a mirror with makeup brushes and paint pots. A makeup master stands behind, holding a palette and brush, about to apply symbolic colors. On the mirror, a face-pattern chart shows different opera characters. A role card and a call sheet lie nearby. Text on Face-pattern chart on mirror reads exactly: "霸王别姬·项王
额上一弯白，谓之通天。眼旁紫红晕染，示其刚烈。
花脸谱式，重在传神。项王以黑为本，额画通天纹，以示其霸。眼窝紫红，暗含悲愤。眉梢上挑，显其英武。
霸王脸谱，玄色为主，示其刚猛。额间通天纹，一道白光直贯发际，喻其气概凌云。眼窝以紫红晕染，状其郁结悲愤。双眉画作卧蚕，眉梢微挑，含英武之姿。谱式未可草率，务求神完气足。
项王脸谱之玄色，须选上等油烟墨调以蛋清，以增其亮泽。紫红眼窝当取胭脂与朱砂相和，自内眼角向外缓缓晕开，渐次淡去，方显郁结之气。勾画轮廓时，笔锋宜沉稳，一鼓作气，方能不滞不涩。". Text on Role card on dressing table reads exactly: "项王，黑膛脸，肃目，忠勇无双

prompt_en:
An alley is decorated with colorful handmade lanterns hanging on strings overhead. Families walk and pause beneath them. A wooden table near an entrance holds an answer ledger and a brush. A welcome board stands at the alley entrance. The lanterns sway slightly in the breeze. Text on Lantern riddles reads exactly: "一川橫贯，两岸孤直，无翼而飞，见者皆谜。(打一字)
一船载米，一船载盐，两头尖尖。
一轮明月挂中天，三五良宵共团圆。
四四方方一座城，里面住着百万兵，只见兵打仗，不见兵出城。
红纸灯笼下系谜笺，字迹娟秀。另有灯谜数则，或咏物，或拆字，皆寓吉祥之意。猜者须细心揣摩，不可妄猜。
另有谜云：“此物生来圆又亮，夜晚行路最帮忙，家家户户都需它，一到天明就下岗。”". Text on Answer ledger reads exactly: "谜底：川——三笔相映，象形若流
谜底：菱。
谜底：明月之情，团圆之意。
谜底：蜂巢。
今夜猜谜者众，已录得以下谜底：灯谜一谜底为“川”，因其三笔横竖相映，似水流之形；灯谜二谜底为“菱”，取其两头尖尖之貌；灯谜三乃咏“明月”，寓团圆之意；灯谜四为“蜂巢”，因其内藏万兵，进出忙碌，恰似兵士守城。
谜底为灯笼，取其光照黑夜、夜行引路之用，诚与灯节相契。
灯谜五谜底：“竹”，因其中空有节，似君子谦逊；灯谜六谜底：“墨斗”，木匠用以取直，暗喻规矩。
灯谜七谜底：“秤”，权衡轻重，持家以平；灯谜八谜底：“伞”，能屈能伸，遮风挡雨。
灯谜九谜底：“钟”，晨昏报时，警醒世人；灯谜十谜底：“镜”，正衣冠，明得失。
另有灯谜数十则，谜底或为日常器物，或为自然风物，皆含劝勉之意，望猜者細味。". Text on Welcome board at alley entrance reads exactly: "元宵灯谜会·欢迎猜射
今晚共悬百谜，猜中三谜可领花灯一盏。
孩童需大人陪同，灯下勿近火烛。
灯谜会设于坊巷，以彰文雅。凡猜中者，持谜笺至账房对奖。孩童须由大人带领，共赏花灯。
灯谜会规则：每户限猜五谜，多猜不计；谜底须当面揭晓，中者当场记录。". A parent reads a riddle on a lantern aloud to a child, while another person writes the answer in the answer ledger. An elderly visitor points at a lantern and smiles, and a girl runs from one lantern to another. The welcome board is visible in the background.

title_en: Classical Raga Lesson with Notation and Annotation
title_zh: 古典拉格课堂：记谱与批注
prompt_en:
A rehearsal room in a music school. A singing teacher stands beside a wooden notation board, holding a chalk. On the board, five ascending phrases are written in staff notation with Arabic numerals below, and red chalk marks outline the grace-note pattern. A student sits cross-legged with a paper lyric sheet in Hindi, and the tabla player has a small card with the tala cycle. Text on wooden notation board reads exactly: "Raga Yaman – Arohana: N R G M P D N S' | Ornament: Mind (grace)
Avaroha: S' N D P M G R S | Vadi: G, Samvadi: N | Jati: Sampurna-Sampurna
Second phrase: M G R S. In Yaman, R is komal (flat), giving the raga its signature. The mind (grace) typically touches the vadi G with oscillation.". Text on lyric sheet reads exactly: "जो तुम तन मन ध्यावो | श्री राम सदा सहायो
तान: सा रे ग म प ध नि सां | आलाप: सा रे सा
ध्यान से गाओ, स्वर साफ रखो।". Text on tala card reads exactly: "Teental: 4+4+4+4 | Sam on 1
Vibhag: dha | kha | ga | dha | Bols: dha dhin dhin dha | dha dhin dhin dha | dha tin tin ta | ta dhin dhin dha". The teacher taps the board at the second phrase and sings a short ascending figure, then circles the grace-note mark. The student sings the phrase back, slightly flat, and the teacher nods and underlines a numeral while explaining. The tabla player counts a 16-beat cycle and the student joins again with more accurate ornamentation.

Midway, he flips to the movement cue sheet and gestures for the dancers to enter the roda, timing their cartwheels to the response phrase.

prompt_en:
A cozy artisan's studio table. The henna artist and bride sit together with an open design folio containing watercolor motif sketches and a motif explanation sheet. A themed consent card lies beside them. The bride points to a peacock-and-paisley motif, and the artist carefully reads a note on the consent card before sketching. Text on design folio reads exactly: "Motif: Peacock – joy and new beginnings | Border: Paisley – eternity
Design: peacock with flowing tail feathers, paisley border, small lotus near base, trailing vines
Peacock tail has seven eyes; pattern repeats over the bride's hand and arm.". Text on motif explanation sheet reads exactly: "Ganesha: remover of obstacles | Lotus: purity, resilience | Mango: fertility
Peacock feathers symbolize the couple's love; paisley represents blessings; vines indicate growth in marriage.
Jasmine stands for divine hope; marigold for passion; the combination brings prosperity.". Text on consent card reads exactly: "Terms: no names, no hidden text, black only
Client may request hidden symbols; confirm placement and ink color before starting. All motifs natural.
Small symbols for luck are allowed inside paisley swirls.". The bride opens the folio and gestures to a peacock encircled with paisley borders. The artist turns the consent card and underlines the instruction 'no names hidden' in gold ink. After a short discussion, the artist draws a small peacock outline on the bride's wrist, while the bride traces a motif in the folio that she associates with her grandmother's story.

A dim backstage room at a cultural festival. A bard in traditional robes reviews a stack of handwritten cue cards, while a musician tunes a string instrument. On a small table lie a refrain sheet and a printed performance program. Text on cue card reads exactly: "第七折 渡江遇险 水怪现形 唤铁桥

唱：惊涛裂岸，浊浪排空，孤舟一叶，性命悬丝。水怪狰狞，掀波作浪，英雄未至，众人惶惶。
白：却说那铁桥公，本名赵铁桥，自幼习得一身好水性，善使一柄铁桨。今番途经此江，见妖风骤起，便知有异。
白：赵铁桥立船头，喝道：‘何方妖孽，胆敢在此兴风作浪！’水怪咆哮，翻起巨浪。铁桥提起铁桨，跳入江中，与怪缠斗。说时迟那时快，铁桥一桨击中水怪天灵，江水翻腾，终于平静。
白：铁桥公奋起神威，一挥铁桨，但见金光万道，水怪跌入江心，不多时，浪平江静。众乡民齐声欢呼，争相上前拜谢。铁桥公拱手道：‘此乃分内之事，乡里平安，吾愿足矣。’". Text on refrain sheet reads exactly: "铁桥镇河 浪静风平 英雄名 万古传
铁桥护民 五谷丰登 香火永续 岁岁平安
第二段：铁桥功成，江上立庙，四时祭祀，福泽乡里。
第三段：自此之后，江上再无妖患，乡民感念其德，立庙以祀。". Text on performance program reads exactly: "戌时开演 说书人 李长河 鼓乐相伴
曲目：铁桥公传奇 第七、八折
（开场白）列位看官，且听我慢慢道来。此乃本地流传百年的铁桥公斩蛟故事，今宵专演渡江与显圣二折，以飨乡里。

prompt_en:
In a quiet sunlit room, a row of low wooden tables. On the nearest table lies a broken ceramic bowl colored dark blue, its fragments already joined with gleaming gold lacquer lines. Next to the bowl rests an open paper ledger, its pages filled with handwriting and small sketches. On the wall above the table hangs a cork board with a handwritten process guide and polaroid photos of repaired vessels. Small jars of gold powder and brushes line the tabletop. Text on repair ledger reads exactly: "欠けた記憶を金で繋ぐ: The bowl we repair still holds the story.
修復の記録: 割れた縁は祖母の声を、ひびの奥には母の笑い声が残る。この茶碗は三代の朝を支えてきた。金の線は過去を隠さず、未来を照らす。私たちの手は記憶を繋ぎ、器は再び家族の食卓に並ぶ。". Text on process board reads exactly: "1. 清掃/clean 2. 接合/join 3. 金継ぎ/kintsugi 4. 納得/accept — Every crack is a chapter.
Every crack is a chapter in the vessel's life; joining with gold honors each break and makes the whole stronger than before. The process requires patience: clean the edges, align the shards, apply the lacquer, and accept the unique seam.". Text on object story card reads exactly: "祖母の茶碗: 今もまだ家族の声を包んでいる。
祖母が毎朝お茶を入れてくれた。欠けた部分は彼女の優しさだった。今、金の線はその声を包み、私たちに微笑む。". A participant gently turns the repaired bowl in her hands. Dipping a fine brush into gold-tinged lacquer, she traces a hairline crack to perfect the seam, then sets down the brush. She opens the ledger and writes what the repaired object will continue to hold. A companion at the same table reads the process board aloud, then adds his own note to the ledger, pointing to the dried gold line as they talk.

A sunlit room in a rural home. An elderly grandmother and her adult granddaughter sit at a wooden table with an old embroidered cloth spread out. The cloth displays rows of traditional motifs: a pine tree, a crane, a lotus, and a pair of fish, each with tiny Chinese characters stitched beneath. A small handwritten note card lies beside the cloth, describing a new motif to add. The grandmother points to a symbol, while the granddaughter holds a needle and thread. Text on embroidered cloth reads exactly: "松鹤延年
莲年有鱼
松: 常青、長寿、不変。鶴: 千年を生き、天と地を結ぶ。蓮: 清らかさ、泥より出でて染まらず。魚: 豊穣、調和、余裕。
松鶴同春，寓意長壽與吉祥；蓮年有魚，諧音「連年有餘」，祈求年年富足。
鶴壽千年，松柏長青，蓮出淨水，魚躍有餘。
松针四季常青，象征长寿；鹤飞九天，寓意高洁；莲花出淤泥而不染，表清白家声；双鱼戏水，愿子孙绵延，年年有余。
松樹象徵長壽，鶴鳥代表高潔，蓮花喻清白，雙魚兆豐年，四紋合為“壽、潔、清、裕”。
祖母指紋樣，歷數家史：松為祖輩手植，鶴為遷居祥兆，蓮出於祖宅池塘，魚盼年年有餘。
繡法以平針、套針、打籽繡為主，線色深淺過渡，恰如水墨暈染。
邊框處預留空位，將補繡梅瓣五朵，每瓣藏一“福”字，合“五福臨門”之吉。
祖母囑咐：紋樣不僅求美，更承家訓——守正、篤學、勤儉、和睦、知恩。". Text on handwritten note card reads exactly: "梅开五福
梅開五福: 梅花五瓣、それぞれ福禄寿喜財を表す。冬に咲き、希望と再生の象徴。この縁取りに加える。
今日補繡梅瓣，願家人平安、事業順遂，福氣隨春而至。
五福臨門，春滿庭院。
今補梅花，表吾家願。
梅花寒冬綻放，寓堅韌不拔；五瓣象徵五福，繡入布緣，願家族綿延，福澤長久。
紙箋角落畫有小梅枝，旁註：取東坡“梅破春近”之意，繡時須留意花瓣向背。". The grandmother explains the meaning of each motif as she points with her finger, tracing the pine tree, crane, lotus, and fish symbols. The granddaughter listens and then looks at the note card, which shows a sketch of a plum blossom and the words (plum blooms with five blessings). She picks up the needle and begins to stitch a new plum blossom motif onto the cloth's border, while the grandmother watches approvingly.

title_en: The Family Stamp: A Ceremonial Bread Gathering
title_zh: 家族印记：仪式面包聚会
prompt_en:
In a rustic bakery's stone-walled workshop, three generations of bakers gather around a long oak table. A wooden stamp index rack displays carved stamps with handles shaped like wheat sheaves. On the table, a linen-covered board holds rows of unbaked dough rounds, each brushed with egg wash. A chalkboard menu on the wall lists the day's specials. The morning light filters through a dusty window. Text on wooden stamp index rack reads exactly: "Harvest Blessing · Midsummer Swirl · Ancestor Knot · New Dawn Braid
Harvest Blessing: wheat sheaf design for the autumn gathering; Midsummer Swirl: spiral honoring the sun's peak; Ancestor Knot: interwoven lines remembering family roots; New Dawn Braid: three-strand plait for the spring renewal.". Text on gathering notice (handwritten card) reads exactly: "Autumn Communion Feeds All — bring your stamp
Every stamp carries its story: the Harvest Blessing feeds the hungry, the Midsummer Swirl marks the longest day, the Ancestor Knot binds generations, and the New Dawn Braid welcomes the new season. Families bring their own stamps to imprint their prayers.". Text on dough board (linen cover) reads exactly: "Pressed with love, risen with faith
Each loaf carries a family's blessing for the table.". The eldest baker lifts a carved stamp from the rack, presses it into a dough round, then hands it to a young woman who sprinkles coarse salt over the imprinted loaf. A middle-aged man consults a handwritten gathering notice and reads aloud the occasion each stamp represents. They discuss the sayings carved on the handles.

title_en: Gilding the Name: An Apprentice's Lesson
prompt_en:
A sunlit workshop with high ceilings is filled with the scent of varnish and linseed oil. The master sign painter stands before a large wooden storefront sign propped on easels, its surface coated with red sizing. The apprentice, wearing a smock, watches closely. Nearby, a workbench holds numbered jars of gold leaf and a handwritten technique card. A sketch sheet with the storefront lettering and flourishes lies beside the sign. Text on storefront sign reads exactly: "VELVET & VINE — Established 1923 — Purveyors of Fine Hats
Velvet & Vine: Since 1923, we have outfitted the city's finest gentlemen and ladies with hats crafted from the softest velour and the most resilient straw, each blocked by hand and finished with silk ribbons.". Text on technique card (handwritten card) reads exactly: "Sizing: 4 hours tack · Leaf: sealer first · Shadow: dry brush
Sizing must reach a tack of four hours before leaf will adhere; always apply a sealer to the sized surface, then lay each leaf with a gentle touch, and finish the letter with a dry-brush shadow to give depth.". Text on sketch sheet reads exactly: "Keep the 'V' strong, let the vine twine
Let the V rise with bold diagonal force while the vine curls softly around it, in the spirit of our house style.". The master uses a gilder's tip to lift a delicate square of gold leaf, presses it onto the sized letter, and burnishes it with a soft brush. He points to the technique card, explaining the sequence of sizing, leafing, and shadowing. The apprentice traces the letterforms on the sketch sheet with a graphite stick.

A small notepad lies open with a measurement comparison and a test checklist. Secure loose objects. Heavy rain likely. Avoid outdoor activities.". Text on Sketch-style floor plan taped to the sliding glass door reads exactly: "INDOOR SAFE ZONES: Kitchen counter (low light, ok for herbs). Living room window (bright, ok for citrus). Text on Checklist on the sliding door next to the map reads exactly: "TO MOVE NOW: Basil (light, Sarah). Mint (light, Tom). Rosemary (medium, Mom). TRAY: Move inside immediately. CITRUS: Stay put. CHECK: All windows closed?". Text on Small sticky note on the plastic tray reads exactly: "TRAY: Loose! Move to kitchen sink. Do not leave on railing.". They mark the herbs as 'move now' and assign tasks. They cross out the tray from the 'keep outside' list and move it inside. They update the floor plan to reflect the new positions.

title_en: The Stain That Kept the Record
prompt_en:
A narrow second-floor hallway under a water-stained ceiling. A brownish crescent spreads from a small opening, with masking-tape flags marking its edge. Beneath it, a low bookshelf holds a plastic bin and stacked towels. A note is taped to the wall near the thermostat, and an envelope scrap is tucked into the bathroom doorframe. Under the sink, two chrome shutoff handles are visible with a tag tied to one. Text on 3x5 index card taped to the wall below the thermostat reads exactly: "Noah — Leak found Sat 6:15 above blue tape. I closed both shutoffs under Mara's sink. Stain passed pencil line by Monday. Keep towels on floor line; do not use upstairs tub until Dave fixes drain. Call if drip returns before you open valve. —Yuki". Text on torn envelope margin tucked into the bathroom doorframe reads exactly: "Yuki — Roof vent clear. Left valve is tub's cold feed. Turn clockwise only. I'll bring bucket Tuesday and replace drain flange. —Dave". Text on graph-paper sketch taped to the bookshelf reads exactly: "X = towels
white chalk line = dry zone
bucket under blue mark
water trails to corner". Text on twist-tie tag looped around the chrome shutoff under the bathroom sink reads exactly: "BATH COLD — CLOSED 6:20". Text on masking-tape flag stuck to the stained ceiling edge reads exactly: "SAT 6:15". Yuki studies the taped note, then uses a pencil to trace the newest outline of the stain on the ceiling. Noah crouches below the sink, reads the tag on the left valve, and turns its handle clockwise. He then picks up the folded towels and places them along the drawn boundary on the floor, following the graph-paper sketch on the bookshelf.

prompt_en: A bright third-floor apartment hallway during a friend-assisted move. Packing boxes line the walls. A large sheet of paper with a text list is taped to the back of the white front door. A clipboard hangs from a coat hook on the wall near the kitchen. By the elevator door, a yellow sticky note marks a booking window. Text on the paper list taped to the inside of the front door reads exactly: "ROOM PLAN — KITCHEN: FOOD & DISHES. LIVING ROOM: BOOKSHELF BOXES. BATH: TOWELS ONLY. BEDROOM 1 = JO'S ROOM. BEDROOM 2 = MIRA'S ROOM. CARRY BOXES TO THE CORRECT DOOR, DO NOT UNPACK. ELEVATOR BOOKED 3:00–3:50. IF A LABEL SAYS THE WRONG ROOM, FIX IT BEFORE CARRYING.". Text on a large, bold, white adhesive label on a cardboard moving box reads exactly: "BEDROOM 1 → BEDROOM 2 — MIRA'S DESK LAMP + CHARGER, FRAGILE, DO NOT STACK". Text on the clipboard hanging on the wall reads exactly: "FRAGILE BOX LOG — LAMP B2 ✓, MIRROR B2, GLASSES KITCHEN, PRINTER LIVING ROOM, JO'S TOOLBOX BEDROOM 1. CHECK EACH BOX BEFORE IT LEAVES THE DOOR.". Text on a yellow sticky note beside the elevator call button reads exactly: "ELEVATOR WINDOW 3:00–3:50 — SEND BIG BOXES NOW.". Mira compares the label on a large box to the layout on the door, spots that the printed destination is one room off, and rewrites the destination with a marker. She then ticks the lamp entry on the clipboard checklist. Jo lifts the corrected box and carries it down the hall to the room assigned to Mira, while Sam glances at the elevator note before heading out.

scene_type: shared-laundry rescue for a delicate garment
title_en: The Silk Blouse Rescue in the Basement Laundry
title_zh: 地下洗衣房里的真丝衬衫救援
prompt_en: In a basement laundry room, a white top-loading washer is stopped with its clear lid open, revealing a dusty-rose silk blouse inside. A handwritten note card is pinned above the machines, a sewn care label is visible inside the blouse collar, a paper sign-up card is clipped to the washer, and a fabric tag hangs from a white basket nearby. A neighbor stands by the open washer, looking at the blouse inside. Text on handwritten note card pinned above the washers reads exactly: "For whoever sees this. I left my dusty-rose silk blouse in a white basket by Machine 2 after treating a coffee stain on the collar. It is delicate. Do NOT run hot or spin. Please set Machine 3 to Cold + Delicates + No Spin, add gentle soap from the shelf, and write below. — Mara, Apt 4C". Text on sewn care label inside the blouse collar reads exactly: "100% silk. Dry clean only. Cool iron. No bleach. Do not tumble.". Text on paper sign-up card clipped to the washer reads exactly: "Laundry sign-up. Monday 7:30 M. 4A; 8:15 L. 2B; 9:00 P. 5C. Start only your slot.". Text on fabric tag tied to a white basket reads exactly: "Mara 4C — silk blouse — coffee stain — vinegar + cold water — no dryer". The neighbor reaches into the washer to lift the blouse, checks the sewn care label and the handwritten note, reads the sign-up card to confirm whose load was spinning, then resets the dial on the other washer to a cold, gentle, no-spin program, places the blouse in the white basket, and writes a reply line on the note card.

prompt_en: A single, wide shot of a compact mudroom just inside a back door with a tiled floor, a wooden bench, coat hooks, a wall shelf, and a dog bed. A red leash hangs beside a clearly visible laminated feeding card; a paper medication packet with a prominent veterinary label rests on the shelf, a handwritten route note is clipped to a corkboard above the cabinet, and a labeled green kibble bin stands on the floor. A frog-shaped planter sits on the porch step beside the door. Text on handwritten note on ruled paper tucked under a magnetic clip on the cabinet door reads exactly: "Evening plan changed — work pickup moved to 5:30. Feed Miso at 6:00, not 5:00. Text on laminated feeding card propped on the shelf next to the bowl reads exactly: "Miso feeding card — evening: one scoop green-bag kibble at 6:00 PM. No treats. Water bowl full.". Text on veterinary label taped to the paper medication packet reads exactly: "Miso — Petofin 25 mg — half tablet at night with food — keep refrigerated.". Text on handwritten walking-route note clipped to the corkboard reads exactly: "Sycamore loop: blue gate, left at the big maple, around the sycamore, back. Not the park trail — muddy. Poop bags in red leash pocket.". Text on adhesive label on the green kibble bin reads exactly: "Evening bag — Miso only". The pet owner hands the neighbor the red leash, then points to the evening feeding time on the laminated card. The owner places the paper medication packet on the shelf next to the feeding card. The neighbor reads the clipped route note, checks the side pocket of the leash, then picks up the porch key and tucks it under the frog-shaped planter as the owner nods.

prompt_en: At a wooden dining table in a compact apartment, a young couple sits across from each other. Thank you for paying on time.". Text on handwritten agreement note reads exactly: "We agreed: keep Gift $80 untouched. Move $35 from Food and $25 from Transport to cover the utility bill. Remaining Food = $215.". Text on grocery receipt reads exactly: "GreenMart 3/22: bread $3.20, milk $4.15, eggs $3.60, coffee $8.75. Total $19.70.". Text on revised budget slip reads exactly: "April cash plan: Utilities $214.70, Food $215, Transport $60, Gift $80. Total $569.70. Signed R + L.". The partners compare the utility bill's higher-than-expected amount against the handwritten agreement. One points at the protected Gift envelope, then uses a pencil to revise the allocation on a blank slip. The other checks the grocery receipt and nods, adjusting the Food line. The revised slip is placed into the envelope sleeve.

title_en: The Sunflowers That Replaced the Roses
prompt_en: In a bright home kitchen, two women and a man gather around a counter where a plain bakery box sits open. A bakery order worksheet lies next to a clipped handwritten note, and an ingredient tag hangs from the cake box on a short string beside a small receipt. One woman lifts the cake slightly; the other compares the note with the flower decoration around the cake. The man turns the tag and checks the written order number, then picks up the receipt. Text on bakery order worksheet reads exactly: "Maple & Sage Bakery — Order #M-4217 — Pickup Sat May 10, 3:00 PM — 8-inch carrot cake with cream cheese frosting, one dozen pale pink buttercream roses around the rim, hand-lettered message 'Happy 71st, Grandma Rosa' — almond-free requested; changes only by written note; $12 deposit paid, $24 balance at pickup; no substitutions please.". Text on handwritten change-request note reads exactly: "Change decoration: pale pink roses to golden sunflowers; keep 'Happy 71st, Grandma Rosa'; same almond-free carrot cake. — Lidia. Handed to counter clerk May 8, 6:40 PM; if impossible, call (555) 014-7719 before 8 PM.". Text on ingredient tag tied to cake box reads exactly: "Maple & Sage — carrot cake, cream cheese frosting; contains dairy and wheat; prepared in a kitchen that handles nuts, but this cake is almond-free and contains no walnuts; order M-4217; best by May 11; keep refrigerated; remove 30 minutes before serving; do not freeze.". Text on payment receipt reads exactly: "M-4217 — deposit $12 paid — balance $24 due at pickup — thank you.". The cake is decorated with golden sunflowers around the rim, reflecting the change request. The woman holding the note taps the sunflower decoration around the cake and nods, showing her sister that the requested change is correct. Her sister lays the order worksheet flat and traces the order number on it; the man aligns the ingredient tag with the receipt and points to the remaining balance, confirming this is still the cake they asked for before the family closes the box for the celebration.

Text on Freezer-door inventory sheet reads exactly: "Freezer Inventory — Updated 3/16. Red Lentil Soup: 2 portions, 3/08, eat first. Chickpea Coconut Stew: 2 portions, 3/14. Vegetable Fried Rice: 1 portion, 3/10. Spinach Lasagna: 2 portions, 3/09 — eaten Tue. Pesto Pasta: 1 portion, 3/15. If in doubt, check lid labels.". Text on Meal-plan note held by a fridge magnet reads exactly: "Monday dinner: warm Red Lentil Soup together with Vegetable Fried Rice. Pull from freezer before 5pm. Do not open new containers.". Text on Small laminated card clipped to freezer shelf reads exactly: "Eat first: Red Lentil Soup, made 3/08, two bowls left. Do not use other soups yet.". They lift the lids, confirm the portions by sight, and combine the contents of the older labeled container with the contents of the second labeled container into one larger bowl for tonight's meal.

prompt_en: Inside a living room, a family of four is gathered around a large freshwater aquarium on a wooden stand. The water is slightly cloudy and a faint green algae film covers parts of the glass. A small dry-erase board sits on the stand, and a laminated care sheet is taped to the hood. An open spiral logbook rests on the edge of the stand beside a siphon hose and a water-conditioner bottle. A sticky note is attached to the lid above the waterline. Text on Dry-erase board on the aquarium stand reads exactly: "FEED EVERY OTHER DAY — SKIP FRIDAY". Text on Laminated care sheet taped to the hood reads exactly: "TWENTY PERCENT WATER CHANGE EVERY SUNDAY. VACUUM GRAVEL. WIPE INSIDE GLASS. RINSE FILTER SPONGE IN REMOVED TANK WATER. NEVER WASH FILTER SPONGE UNDER TAP WATER.". Text on Handwritten logbook open on the stand reads exactly: "Tue Oct 8 — Pearl hovered near surface. Did early 25% water change. Removed 20 L. Added 10 mL conditioner. Rinsed siphon. Next change: Sun Oct 13.". Text on Water-conditioner bottle label reads exactly: "WATER CONDITIONER — Removes chlorine and chloramine. Dose: 5 mL per 10 gallons. Add to fresh water before refilling.". Text on Sticky note on the tank lid reads exactly: "RINSE SIPHON BEFORE REUSE — NO SOAP". Noticing the cloudy water and the algae on the glass, the teenager calls the rest of the family over. One parent inspects the laminated care sheet while another reads the most recent logbook entry, which records an early water change from Tuesday after a fish appeared stressed. The family compares those dates with the feeding rules on the dry-erase board and with the dose printed on the water-conditioner bottle. They then mix the conditioner into a bucket of fresh water, use the siphon to remove part of the tank water, and refill the aquarium. When the new logbook entry is written in, the teen erases the old feeding schedule on the board and writes a corrected schedule that all four agree on.

Delgado, Unit 3A, Cedar Ln.". Text on small paper receipt held by the woman reads exactly: "Received by R.Okafor: 1 box, Unit 2B, from Ana Delgado, Unit 3A. 10/14.". The man checks the labels against the log and hands his box to the woman; the woman hands her box to the man. The woman signs the receipt and gives it to the man. Then she steps to the door frame, crosses out the last line of the card, writes an updated line with her pen, and nods.

title_zh: 扁豆炖菜的上层搁板归位
prompt_en:
A small shared community refrigerator sits in a building's common room. A clipboard ledger rests on top of the fridge. Inside, labeled glass containers share shelves with a few bagged items. The lower shelf carries a sticky note, and the upper shelf edge shows a short category label. Text on Clipboard ledger resting on top of the fridge reads exactly: "COMMUNITY FRIDGE — USE-FIRST LOG
Take what you need. Add what you can.
Write date, name, item.
Older food moves to the top shelf.
Mon 9/12 — Tofu curry — Lina — take first
Tue 9/13 — Lentil stew — Maya — keep on top shelf". Text on Handwritten label taped to a glass food container reads exactly: "Maya's Lentil Stew
Vegan — no nuts — no sesame
Ready to eat
Keep on TOP shelf
Best by Fri
Take one". Text on Sticky note on the edge of the lower shelf reads exactly: "Sam — if you see Maya's stew below the top shelf, please move it up. Her label says top only. — Lina". Text on Short label on the top shelf edge reads exactly: "READY TO EAT". A neighbor opens the fridge, reads the sticky note on the lower shelf, checks the handwritten label on a glass container, and then lifts the container up to the top shelf.

title_en: The Folded Message After the Delay
title_zh: 延误之后的那张折叠留言
prompt_en: Two friends sit on a wooden station bench, a tote bag on the bench beside them. On the bench between them is a printed booking page with ticket stubs, a handwritten delay note copied from the departures board, and a folded handwritten message. A small station canopy shelters the platform. The printed booking page lies flat as the central focus, displaying the itinerary clearly. Text on Printed booking page with itinerary and two ticket stubs reads exactly: "Sat 8 Jun — Belldale 10:12 to Fenwick Junction 11:03; Fenwick Junction 11:28 to Ashcombe Central 12:47. Train T2817. Coach C, seats 41A & 41B. Two adults, railcard applied. Ticket stubs: BELDALE → FENWICK JUNCTION · OFF-PEAK DAY RETURN · 2 ADULTS · 08 JUN.". Beside it, a handwritten delay note is held up. Text on Handwritten delay note copied from departure board reads exactly: "Delayed — T2817 Belldale 10:12 now 10:47, arrives Fenwick Junction 11:38. You will miss the 11:28 Ashcombe connection. Ticket staff can rebook you on the next service.". A hand-drawn red line connects the new time on the note to the missed connection on the booking page. A folded message lies nearby. Text on Handwritten lodging message from host reads exactly: "Elena — spare key under the grey pot by the back door. Sofa bed is made up. Fridge has eggs and bread. Call if you're later than six.". One friend points to the red line connecting the delay note to the booking page, then unfolds the message and taps its final line.

The group shoulders their packs and turns away from the upper peak, following their prearranged turnaround condition.

The boy points directly at the envelope on the counter. The mother looks from the clipboard to the map, tracing a route with her finger.

prompt_en: A small front porch has a two-shelf wooden bookcase with paperbacks, a corkboard fixed above it, a woven basket on the floor, and a second smaller basket with a plain tag. Please read The Blue Atlas of Small Tides slowly; the tide table on page 44 is wrong on purpose. When you finish, pass it to Mei at the porch swap — she asked first. Add your name and date below mine.". Text on pale blue request card pinned to the corkboard reads exactly: "Mei asked first for The Blue Atlas of Small Tides. If Ana's copy comes back, leave it in the Return Basket. I will bring back your soup pot on Thursday. — Mei". Text on label taped to the large woven basket reads exactly: "Return Basket — books going to specific readers. Please keep promised titles here.". Text on tag tied to the smaller basket reads exactly: "Hold for Mei — Blue Atlas". The neighbor places the paperback into the large woven basket, then notices the handwritten note on the inside front cover of the book, and reads the request card pinned to the corkboard. She lifts the book from the large basket, sets it into the smaller tagged basket, and smooths the tag onto the book's front edge.

scene_type: living-room stereo reconnection after a cabinet move
prompt_en:
In a living room after a media cabinet has been moved, two housemates kneel among a stereo receiver, turntable, speakers and a box of disconnected leads. Masking-tape cable flags, a hand-drawn shelf diagram and a listening-test notebook lie open beside the cabinet. Text on hand-drawn reconnection map taped inside the cabinet door reads exactly: "STEREO RECONNECT AFTER MOVE
Turntable RCA → PHONO L/R
Thin black ground → GND screw
Blue pair → LEFT speaker red/black
White pair → RIGHT speaker red/black
Connect power last. Test at low volume before closing cabinet.". Text on masking-tape flags wrapped around the loose cable ends reads exactly: "BLUE = LEFT SPEAKER
WHITE = RIGHT SPEAKER
THIN BLACK = TURNTABLE GROUND
RCA RED = RIGHT / RCA WHITE = LEFT". Text on listening-test page open on the floor reads exactly: "TEST RECORD: SIDE A, TRACK 2
First check 19:40 — right channel only; hum present.
Correction — blue to LEFT; black to GND.
Second check 19:47 — both channels clear; hum gone.
Noor + Eli.". Text on small note tucked under the cabinet wheel lock reads exactly: "Before pushing cabinet back: photograph rear panel, leave 8 cm cable slack, lock both front wheels.". They trace each labeled lead against the diagram, discover that the left speaker and turntable ground were swapped during packing, reconnect both, then play the marked test record and write the result before pushing the cabinet back against the wall.

scene_type: houseguest instructions resolve a key and pet mix-up
title_en: The Key That Opens the Door
prompt_en:
A small tiled entryway inside a home, featuring a mirror, a wooden console, and a half-open kitchen doorway. On the console sits a ceramic bowl containing two nearly identical brass keys: one with a red tape tab, the other with a blue tape tab. A white envelope is taped to the mirror. A handwritten index card is clipped to the kitchen gate. A printed recycling calendar is on the refrigerator door. A whiteboard hangs beside the coat hooks. Next to the doorway is a small wooden key rack with two hooks labeled 'FRONT / MAIL'.

The text on the white envelope taped to the mirror must read exactly: "Priya, welcome! The red-taped brass key opens the front door; the blue-taped one opens the mailbox. Walk in, then hang the red key on the hook labeled FRONT and put the blue key in the drawer marked MAIL. I won't be back until six. Keeper is in the kitchen."

The text on the handwritten index card clipped to the kitchen gate must read exactly: "Keeper stays in the kitchen. Don't let him past the gate. He gets his food at five."

The text on the printed recycling calendar on the refrigerator door must read exactly: "Recycling: Paper 2nd Tue; Glass 4th Fri; Green bin weekly. No bag ties."

The text on the whiteboard beside the coat hooks must read exactly: "Mara: back by 6, feed Keeper at 5. Don't wait up. Thanks!"

A guest lifts the envelope from the mirror and reads it. She uses the key with the red tape to unlock the entry door. She steps inside, hangs that key on the left hook of the small key rack, and places the blue-taped key in a drawer beneath the rack. She then reads the handwritten card clipped to the kitchen gate, checks the recycling calendar on the refrigerator, and reads the morning message left on the whiteboard near the coat hooks.

title_en: The Orange Bin Gets Its Odd-Month Check
title_zh: 橙色应急箱的奇数月检查
prompt_en:
A mother and her teenage daughter are kneeling on the tiled floor of a hallway, working with a bright orange emergency bin. The daughter holds a fresh water pack and an oatmeal bar, placing them into the bin. The mother holds a clipboard and writes a check mark on a paper checklist. Their father stands nearby, holding a magnetic note he took from the refrigerator, reading the address aloud to the girls. 

Text on the Laminated inventory sheet clipped to the inside of the orange kit lid must read exactly: "Family Emergency Kit Inventory. Check odd months. Replace only if dated before July 2024 or tester says LOW. Last checked Jan 14. Replace now: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Keep flashlight, whistle, dust mask."

Text on the Paper checklist on the clipboard the mother is holding must read exactly: "Checklist today: 2 water pouches, 4 AA batteries, 1 oatmeal bar. Done: water replaced, batteries tested. Still need: bar. Next check: May 3. If you take something, write here."

Text on the Laminated contact card fixed to the front of the orange bin must read exactly: "Meeting place: Elin's porch, 42 Birch Lane. Wait there until everyone checks in. Bring this kit only if you leave."

Text on the Magnetic note the father is holding (originally from the refrigerator) must read exactly: "Call Maya 555-0192 or Rowan 555-0147. Say: safe, no one hurt."

title_en: Sleepover Sort at the Kitchen Island
prompt_en: A kitchen and the adjoining entryway on a Saturday afternoon. Two parents and three children gather around the kitchen island, where backpacks and snack containers are lined up. She checks the yellow sticky note, swaps Leo's snack for the labeled oat-cracker container, and taps the whiteboard bedtime plan while the children set out their pajamas on the sofa.

A bright home sewing corner on a wooden table. An elderly mentor and a young adult learner sit side by side in front of a classic mechanical sewing machine. Text on pasted paper diagram on the machine body reads exactly: "THREADING 1 Spool 2 Top Guide 3 Tension 4 Take-up 5 Needle

Test results: With tension set to 4, straight stitch length 4.0 produced smooth, even stitches. Tension 5 caused puckering, too tight. Lower tension when sewing thin fabric.
Set tension to 3 for delicate fabrics to avoid puckering. Always test on a scrap piece first. If stitches are loose, increase tension by 1; if tight, decrease by 1. Stitch length 3.0 for medium weight.". Text on cardboard tag hanging from tension dial reads exactly: "TENSION 0 loose – 9 tight default 4
Adjust gradually: one number at a time.". The learner follows the step-by-step threading diagram, leading the thread from the spool through the guides and into the needle eye. The mentor points to the stitch-sample notebook, then turns the tension dial while explaining. The learner sews a few test stitches on a scrap of cloth and writes down the result.

A bright kitchen countertop holds a stainless-steel espresso machine with a portafilter, steam wand, and water tank. Nearby, two housemates stand together. On the machine's front, a small care checklist card is taped with rotating tasks. A dosing label is affixed to the side of the machine's group head. In the background, a wall-mounted maintenance log with a grid and handwritten notes hangs near a cabinet. Text on care checklist card reads exactly: "DAILY: backflush w/ water | WEEKLY: backflush w/ cleaner | MONTHLY: descale | TODAY: water backflush
Daily backflush with water after every 10 brews to remove coffee oils. Weekly backflush with 3g cleaner in a blind basket. Monthly descale with citric acid solution. Today's task: water backflush completed at 10:30 AM.
Clean with water after 10 brews. Use 3g cleaner weekly. Descale monthly.". Text on dosing label reads exactly: "Blind basket cleaner: 3 g per dose
Use 3 grams per blind basket for weekly clean. Not for daily.". Text on maintenance log reads exactly: "DATE 02/15 backflush OK; 02/22 descale due". One housemate removes the portafilter and places it on the drip tray, then inserts a cleaning disc and adds a blind basket. The other housemate refills the water tank, and together they run a backflush cycle. Afterward, the first housemate flips a card on the checklist to mark the task complete, while the second checks the maintenance log and notes the date.
